overall: Tomorrow (Tuesday, July 7) will be a humid, unsettled day in Washington, DC dominated by a slow-moving frontal zone interacting with a tropical air mass, producing patchy fog in the morning, multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms through the day, and mostly cloudy skies that will significantly suppress daytime heating. An active Flood Watch through midnight highlights the elevated moisture and rainfall potential. Northeast winds around 6 mph will reinforce onshore flow and limit temperature recovery.
forecast_obs_notes: Model spread is notably wide: ECMWF (~79.3°F) and HRRR (~79.8°F) are the coolest, clustering near 79-80°F and likely capturing the cloud/rain suppression best; NBM (~81.1°F) and GEM (~82.0°F) are in the middle; GFS (~82.9°F) and WEATHER_COM (~84.9°F) run warmer; the forecast-only model (~87.2°F) is a significant outlier. The obs-informed ensemble (~80.0°F) aligns most closely with ECMWF and HRRR, and given the tropical air mass and persistent cloud cover, the cooler guidance appears most credible.
max_temp_prediction: The active odd-bucket market shows a bimodal, highly uncertain distribution with both 79-80°F and 81-82°F tied at 9.4% — a Tier 4 signal (AVOID per system thresholds). The ensemble E[TMAX] of 80.0°F, corroborated by ECMWF and HRRR, points to the 79-80°F or 81-82°F odd buckets, but the flat distribution and high entropy (2.936) reflect genuine model disagreement driven by how much rain and cloud cover materialize. Best estimate is approximately 80-81°F, skewing slightly above the ensemble mean to account for the NWS narrative high of 86°F and some morning clearing potential, but confidence is LOW.
